top_categories.workout_context: 58ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Axel Merckx Gran Fondo's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before July.
5,577ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
At Axel Merckx Gran Fondo, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Axel Merckx Gran Fondo. Train it until it feels boring.
At mile 60 of 96, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.

Road-specific control matters at Axel Merckx Gran Fondo. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 96 miles.
5,577ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 96 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 5,577ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 96 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.

race_overlay.weather: July in Penticton, British Columbia, Canada. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks before Axel Merckx Gran Fondo. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Axel Merckx Gran Fondo’s 96 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Axel Merckx Gran Fondo. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Race Simulation, and VO2max to prepare you for 96 miles of mixed terrain in Penticton, British Columbia, Canada.
